title: A quasi-excellent Jacobson closed fibre makes a G-ring quasi-excellent
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian G-ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal contained in every maximal ideal of $A$ (the Jacobson radical). If $A/I$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], then $A$ is quasi-excellent. No adic completeness, characteristic, dimension, or universal catenarity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 4.1, printed p.4, proved on printed pp.4–7; a generalization of Brodmann–Rotthaus using weak local uniformization. Used at the start of Theorem 5.1 Step 2, printed p.9.

proof.text: It is enough to prove that every nonzero domain $B$ finite as an $A$-module has a nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ on which all local rings are regular. Indeed, any finite $A$-algebra $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. For a prime $P\subset C$, the images of finite module generators generate $C/P$ as an $A$-module. The asserted domain conclusion for $C/P$, applied to every $P$, makes the regular locus of $C$ open by [lem-exc-regular-locus-open-from-prime-quotients]. Then [lem-per-j2-finite-algebra-criterion] makes $A$ J-2. Together with the given Noetherian G-ring property this is quasi-excellence by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The zero ring and a zero finite algebra have empty spectrum, so their regular-locus requirement is vacuous.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, opening proof paragraph, printed p.6; Stacks 07P9, lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed, and 07PC, lemma-J-2

proof.text: Fix such a domain $B$ and put $J=IB$. Finite module generators also generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] makes $B$ a G-ring, in particular Noetherian. The images of those generators make $B/J$ finite type over $A/I$. It is J-2: a finite list generating a $(B/J)$-algebra $D$, together with those generators of $B/J$, generates $D$ over $A/I$ (substitute polynomial expressions for its coefficients). Hence its regular locus is open by the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring] for $A/I$ and the finite-type definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Also $J$ lies in every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $B$. Otherwise some image of $I$ in the field $B/\mathfrak m$ is nonzero, so $I(B/\mathfrak m)=B/\mathfrak m$. This is a finite $A$-module, generated by the images of the generators of $B$. Since $I$ lies in every maximal ideal of $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] would give $B/\mathfrak m=0$, a contradiction.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, end of printed p.6; Stacks 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, and 00DV, lemma-NAK

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, apply [lem-per-g-ring-alteration-closed-fibre-neighbourhood] to $(B,J,\mathfrak q)$. Obtain $b_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$, covers $\varphi_{\mathfrak q,i}$ of $D(b_{\mathfrak q})$ whose ambient local rings above $V(J)$ are regular, and their specified proper-surjective witnesses. Choose finitely many $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ whose basic opens cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$: if the ideal generated by all $b_{\mathfrak q}$ were proper, a maximal ideal containing it would contradict the choice of its own $b_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $1$ is a finite linear combination of them, and those finitely many elements suffice. Write $\varphi_{j,i}:X_{j,i}\to D(b_j)$ and $p_j:V_j\to D(b_j)$ for the resulting finite data.

For each of the finitely many $\varphi_{j,i}$, apply [lem-sbc-generic-flatness]. Its base $D(b_j)=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/b_j]$ is integral and its map is of finite type, hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact. Obtain a nonempty open $U_{j,i}$ in that base over which it is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], choose a nonempty basic open inside $U_{j,i}$, defined by a nonzero fraction $a_{j,i}/b_j^{n_{j,i}}$. Inside $D(b_j)$ this basic open is $D(a_{j,i})\cap D(b_j)$. Take $c=\prod_{j,i}a_{j,i}\ne0$ in the domain $B$ (the empty product is $1$). Then every $\varphi_{j,i}$ is flat over $D(b_j)\cap D(c)$. This produces a common nonempty open $D(c)$; it does not assert that its points all lie in $V(J)$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, generic flatness paragraph, printed p.7; Stacks 052A, morphisms-proposition-generic-flatness

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p\in D(c)$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ of $B$. We have $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Choose $j$ with $\mathfrak m\in D(b_j)$; then $\mathfrak p\in D(b_j)$ too, since $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Lift $\mathfrak p$ to $v_1\in V_j$ by surjectivity. The proper map $p_j$ is closed by [pqf-lem-proper-closed-map], so $p_j(\overline{\{v_1\}})=\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}$: continuity gives containment in that closure, and closedness gives a closed set containing $\mathfrak p$. Hence lift $\mathfrak m$ to $v_2\in\overline{\{v_1\}}$. Some member $V_{j,i}$ of the witness open cover contains $v_2$, and also $v_1$ because opens are stable under generalization. Their images $x_1,x_2\in X_{j,i}$ satisfy $\varphi_{j,i}(x_1)=\mathfrak p$, $\varphi_{j,i}(x_2)=\mathfrak m$, and $x_2\in\overline{\{x_1\}}$ by continuity.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, last paragraph, and Lemma 4.5, printed pp.6–7 (the two-point case, proved here)

proof.text: Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the closed-fibre regularity clause of [lem-per-g-ring-alteration-closed-fibre-neighbourhood] says that $\mathcal O_{X_{j,i},x_2}$ is regular local. Choose an affine open containing $x_2$; it contains its generalization $x_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the two stalks are localizations of the same affine coordinate ring at primes $P_1\subseteq P_2$. Localizing the second stalk further at the prime induced by $P_1$ gives the first: both rings consist of fractions with denominators outside $P_1$, and the maps send a fraction to that same fraction. Now [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] shows that $\mathcal O_{X_{j,i},x_1}$ is regular local.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, final paragraph, printed p.7; Stacks 0AFS, lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular

proof.text: Because $c\notin\mathfrak p$, Step 4 makes $\varphi_{j,i}$ flat at $x_1$. Thus $B_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{X_{j,i},x_1}$ is a flat local map by [def-weil-flat-morphism], identifying the affine base stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. The target is a regular local ring by Step 6 and hence is Noetherian; the source is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], since $B$ is a G-ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] to conclude that $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local. This holds for every $\mathfrak p\in D(c)$. Since $B$ is a nonzero domain and $c\ne0$, its zero prime belongs to $D(c)$. Therefore $D(c)$ is the nonempty regular open required in Step 1, proving the result.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, concluding sentence, printed p.7; Stacks 00OF, lemma-flat-under-regular, and 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence

tool_uses.why: Generic regular opens on prime quotients imply openness of the regular locus; the unit has no commutative-algebra substitute.
Finite module algebras are finite type and inherit the G-ring property; this is a generic algebra tool.
A finite family of finite-type covers over an integral base becomes flat on one dense open; this is the source route, not a replacement of the perverse unit.
Closedness of the proper witness lifts the two-point specialization chain; a general proper-morphism tool.
Regularity passes from a specialized stalk to its generalization; a general algebra tool.
Noetherianity of B_p checks the source hypothesis of flat-local regular descent.
Descent of regularity along the resulting flat local stalk map; this is the final algebra input of the cited proof.
Checks Noetherianity of the arbitrary finite algebra before applying the prime-quotient regular-locus criterion.
